# Rigidity generated by the existing polarization: explicit test

2026-10-05 UTC. A new counted cross-coupling, not an independently adjusted
cosmic and galactic stiffness. Analytical continuation of the elastic-state
result. No numerical parameter scan is needed for the decisions below.

## The proposed operator and its full variation

Add gamma A2 I(C)/4 to the existing modal energy, gamma>0, with

    A2=(4 pi G Kb)^(-1) integral nu kappa_delta delta^2 |y_delta|^2/2,
    I(C)=tr(C^2)-(tr C)^2/3,
    z=1+gamma I(C)/4.

This changes the quadratic modal stiffness by the factor z. It postulates
that the same polarized modes provide material rigidity. It is not yet a
derived graph interaction. The affine background energy/current and its
unselected abundance remain exactly the assumptions identified in V131.

For normalized modes q_s, weight2s ds and beta_s=1/(gc^2 s^4), their relaxed
equations and energy contribution W are

    z q_s+beta_s |q_s|^2 q_s=h(b),
    W=(4 pi G)^(-1) integral2s ds min_q[z q^2/2+beta_s q^4/4-h.q].

The old unstrained endpoint constant is retained. Do not subtract a different
constant for every strain: that would change the physical energy and work.
Envelope differentiation gives

    W_z=A2>0,
    W_zz=-(4 pi G)^(-1) integral2s ds q_s^2/(z+3 beta_s q_s^2),
    -W_zz<=2 A2/z.

The induced shear modulus at C=I is gamma A2. Unexcited FLRW has q=0 and
A2=0; this operator therefore adds no linear cosmic sound term. At small
source A2=b^2/(8 pi G)+o(b^2). At finite strain the modes, source flux,
chemical derivative and stresses must all be recomputed together. Old
constant-strain force/Solar qualifications do not automatically transfer.

## What is positive, and what has not been proved positive

For C=diag(exp(2sigma),exp(-2sigma),1), c=cosh(2sigma), s=sinh(2sigma),

    z=1+gamma(2c^2-c-1)/3,
    z_sigma=2gamma(4c-1)s/3,
    z_sigmasigma=4gamma(8c^2-c-4)/3,
    E_sigmasigma>=A2[z_sigmasigma-2 z_sigma^2/z].

For the disclosed example gamma=1 and |sigma|<=.1, elementary conservative
bounds give E_sigmasigma>=(28/9)A2>0 whenb!=0. This establishes positivity
of this clamped-source shear-path/modal potential block, not every strain
direction, a uniform soft-mode gap or a complete acoustic-tensor theorem.

Source relaxation matters. In shear coordinates e=dev(C)/2, define
V2=integral2s q_s^2, T2=integral2s q_s^2/H_L, T=integral2s q_s/H_L,
U=integral2s/H_L, P=integral2s q_s, H_L=z+3 beta_s q_s^2. A parallel
local Fourier field variation with f_k=(1+ell^2 k^2)^(-1) has
K=1-f_k^2(h'^2 U+h''P). The radial shear-coordinate Schur condition is

    V2>4(z-1)[T2+f_k^2 h'^2 T^2/K].

The additional negative term must not be erased by keeping b clamped.

An exactly volume-preserving compatible simple shear illustrates the limit:
X1=x+s y, X2=y, X3=z_coordinate, det(partial X)=1. Then
I=2s^2+2s^4/3 and z=1+gamma(s^2/2+s^4/6). At fixed s!=0, weak b and
the local-filter limit, the relaxed total field energy is

    E=constant+b^2(1-1/z)/(8 pi G)+O(|b|^3).

After eliminating the field, the shear-curvature bracket is

    z''-2z'^2/(z-1)
      =-gamma[9+9s^2+(10/3)s^4]/(3+s^2)<0.

For finite f_k replace z-1 in the denominator by z-f_k^2. For small shear,
the negative regime requires approximately1-f_k^2<(3/2)gamma s^2 and
x<<gamma s^2. A real patch must admit that wavelength and state hierarchy.
Source-selected strain could vanish fast enough with x to avoid it; this
is not a proof that every formed solution is unstable. Positive total field
energy is not the same as convexity at a forced/prestrained state.

## Material characteristics impose a separate domain condition

At C=I a transverse displacement has delta n=0 at first order and no
quadratic mixing with the modal fluctuations. Its fixed-background block is

    L_T,2=(n epsilon_n/2c^2)|zeta_T_dot|^2
                           -(gamma A2/2)|grad zeta_T|^2,
    c_T^2/c^2=gamma A2/[m_g n(1+eta)].

This particular decoupled block does not require an instantaneous modal
relaxation approximation. Its inertia is NOT m_g n at finite source.
At fixed n, b->infinity on the unstrained bounded-source branch gives
A2->positive constant but1+eta->0. Everygamma>0 eventually violates a
photon-cone material bound unless accessible states avoid that domain.
The bound is gamma A2<=m_g n(1+eta), not a negative-stiffness diagnosis.
At finite shear the endpoint and kinetic tensor change; the unstrained
formula cannot be reused there. Full constrained characteristics remain open.

## The regular static center is a decisive source-selection check

For a smooth centered clamped filtered source b=b1 R+..., a regular attractive
field Phi'/c^2=g1 R+..., g1>0, and a finite positive reference fraction f,
this proposal gives kappa=K2 R^2+..., k_b=B3 R^3+..., eta=-E3 R^3+....
Insert a smooth radial displacement w=A R+B R^3+... in the actual equation

    [k_b(w'+2w/R)+(4kappa/3)(w'-w/R)]'
             +4kappa(w'-w/R)/R=(Phi/c^2+eta)'.

The leading bulk term is9 A B3 R^2 and the leading shear term is
(56/3)K2 B R^3. Neither balancesg1 R. A particular R log R displacement
can supply it: w=3g1 R log(R/R0)/(20K2), but its density strain diverges
logarithmically. It is not a smooth bounded small-strain equilibrium.
Regular spatial metric corrections do not repair the missing leading term.

This retires the locally generated-rigidity, smooth static small-strain
central realization. It does not exclude a nonlinear rearrangement, flow,
cavity, anisotropic state, altered central field or nonlocal stress. No
shear-curvature grid would establish the failed regular-center premise.

At a symmetric center y=0 but its spatial derivatives may be nonzero. A
material-strain coupling to those derivatives, or a positive average S A2,
could yield central rigidity. Neither is already supplied by the present
action: the material-label dependence, metric/filter variation and source
work would be a new constitutive premise. Do not quietly add it as a repair.

Root and both analytical reviewers independently checked complementary
variations and restrictions. These are analytical candidate decisions, not
external peer review, formation evidence or an observational exclusion.
The shared-model problem remains open. A separate compact-galaxy test can
now check whether the adopted100pc filtering scale itself is compatible with
stellar kinematics, without waiting for another elastic completion.
